title: Set With Instant Random Pick
statement:
Build a set of integers that supports three operations, each in O(1) average time:

  • insert(val) adds val if it is not already there. Returns true if it was added, false if it was already present.
  • remove(val) deletes val if it is there. Returns true if it was removed, false if it was missing.
  • getRandom() returns one of the current values, with every value equally likely. It is only called when the set is not empty.

Tests are a list of operations and their arguments; the first one creates the empty set. Because getRandom is random, the checker accepts any value that is in the set at that moment, and on long runs of getRandom over a small set it also checks that every value shows up.

examples.out: [null, true, true, false, true, 9, true, false]
examples.why: The second insert of 4 is refused. After 4 is removed, only 9 is left, so getRandom must return 9. Removing 7 fails because it was never added.
Either 1 or 2 is correct here, each with probability 1/2.

constraints: getRandom is only called on a non-empty set
hints: A hash set gives O(1) insert and remove, but picking a random element from it needs an index. Which structure gives O(1) random access by index?
Keep the values in an array, so getRandom is just a random index. The trouble is removing from the middle of the array.
Also keep a map from value to its index in the array. To remove, copy the last element into the hole, fix its index in the map, and pop the end.

explain.intuition:
Each standard structure covers only part of the job. A hash set inserts and removes in O(1) but has no "give me item number 7" operation, so a uniform random pick needs a full walk. An array picks a random index in O(1), but deleting from its middle shifts everything after it.

The trick is that the array does not need to keep any order. To delete a value, overwrite its slot with the last value and pop the end. Nothing shifts. A map from value to array index tells you where the hole is, and you update the moved value's index in the map. The array stays dense, so every slot is equally likely to be picked.
steps: Keep an array vals and a map pos from value to its index in vals.
insert(v): if v is in pos, return false. Otherwise set pos[v] = vals.length, push v, return true.
remove(v): if missing, return false. Otherwise let i = pos[v] and last be the final element. Write last into vals[i], set pos[last] = i, pop the array, delete v from the map.
pitfalls: Deleting v from the map before updating pos[last]. When v is itself the last element, the order matters: update first, delete second, or the stale entry survives.
Using splice or list.remove to delete from the middle. That is O(n) and breaks the requirement.
Converting the set to an array inside getRandom. It is correct but O(n) per call.

solutions.title: Hash set, copied to an array on each pick
solutions.idea: Insert and remove are direct set operations. getRandom turns the set into an array and picks an index, which is O(n).

solutions.title: Array plus index map, swap with last
solutions.idea: The array gives O(1) random access. The map finds a value's slot, and removing moves the last element into that slot so nothing shifts.

followups: Allow duplicates: insert always adds a copy, and getRandom picks each copy with equal probability. What does the index map store now?
getRandom should pick values with probability proportional to a weight given at insert time. How would you do that?
